scope: All findings remain syntax_hint. Compiler acceptance of a fixture proves syntax/API call validity, never user control, sink reachability, exploitability or sanitizer sufficiency.
default_policy: Enable only replace-escaping and cmark-unsafe as narrow opt-out hints; retain other rules as explicit opt-in review aids.

rules.trigger: replace with security-character literal old/new labelled arguments
rules.real_evidence: Builtin String API calls compile; runtime oracle confirms << becomes << with replace and << with replace_all.
limitations: Dot receiver type is unresolved
User type named String or Dummy.replace can be safe and still match
No proof that output reaches HTML or input is untrusted
rules.wording: Call named replace with an escaping-shaped replacement. If this resolves to builtin String::replace, only the first occurrence is replaced; review receiver identity and output context.

rules.trigger: render/from_doc/renderer/xhtml_renderer called with literal safe=false and cmark import-name hint
rules.real_evidence: cmark 0.4.8 render safe=false/true/default compiled in real-library matrix; separate second-library runtime validation
limitations: Import substring does not establish declaration identity
A local render function can match
Disabling safe mode does not establish untrusted HTML reaching a browser
rules.wording: Rendering-shaped call sets safe=false. For the reviewed cmark API this allows raw HTML; confirm API identity and trust boundary.

rules.trigger: inner_html method with nonliteral/non-uppercase-ident argument and rabbita import-name hint
rules.real_evidence: rabbita 0.15.5 source html/attrs.mbt and svg/attrs.mbt assigns innerHTML; no compiled library fixture in this audit
limitations: Receiver declaration unresolved
Variables holding safe constants still match
Uppercase variable name is not a safety proof
No DOM insertion reachability
rules.wording: Method named inner_html receives an expression. Confirm it is a raw HTML API and inspect where its input originates.

rules.trigger: html call with interpolation plus source text hint and mocket/crescent import-name hint
rules.real_evidence: mocket 0.9.1 HTML interpolation calls compile; trusted local constant interpolation still matches
limitations: No response-return proof
No source provenance
No encoding semantics
No declaration binding
rules.wording: HTML-shaped call contains string interpolation. Review API identity, input origin, output context and whether this response is returned.

rules.trigger: embedded JS or unspecified-language FFI code contains eval( or new Function text
rules.real_evidence: Actual JS extern eval and identity compile with JS target
limitations: Comment containing eval(input) triggers
No JavaScript parser
Whitespace and aliases can evade matching
No user-control evidence
rules.wording: Embedded code contains eval/new Function-shaped text. Confirm executable JavaScript and whether untrusted input reaches it.

rules.trigger: set_header/add_header/append_header/set_response_header with nonliteral second positional or value-labelled argument
rules.real_evidence: Current crescent source has HttpResponse.header, outside matched name set. Real-library fixture compilation is blocked by old lexscan in cookie.mbt; no real sink or CRLF behavior validated.
limitations: No validated current-library matched sink
Safe values in locals trigger
No knowledge of library rejection/normalization
Does not match current crescent header API
rules.wording: Dynamic header-shaped argument. Confirm API identity and CRLF rejection at the real serialization boundary.

rules.trigger: handle_cors/append_cors_headers/append_cors_preflight_headers with credentials=true and no literal non-wildcard origin
rules.real_evidence: Real mocket calls compile; implementation emits wildcard headers. WHATWG Fetch rejects wildcard sharing for credentials=include.
limitations: Original credential theft claim is false for wildcard+credentials alone
Dynamic trusted origin can match
No browser behavioral or reflected-origin proof
No declaration binding
rules.wording: CORS-shaped call combines credentials=true with wildcard or unresolved origin. Browsers reject credentialed wildcard response sharing; review intended origin policy, reflected origins and availability.

rules.trigger: set_cookie method omits one of http_only, secure, same_site labels and mocket/crescent import hint
rules.real_evidence: Real mocket 0.9.1 missing/true/false attribute calls compile
limitations: False attributes are treated as present/safe
Cookie role and deployment are unknown
No serialization inspection
Same-name harmless APIs trigger
rules.wording: Cookie-shaped call omits explicit security attribute labels. Review actual values, cookie purpose and library defaults.

rules.trigger: serve/listen/serve_async call lacks selected direct labels; source also contains .post/.put/.patch and crescent import hint
rules.real_evidence: Crescent 0.11.0 source uses NativeServeOptions(max_request_body_bytes=...); bounded and unbounded calls both match syntax. The real library rejects the fixed compiler due to old lexscan in cookie.mbt, so API calls are not compiler-verified in this audit.
limitations: Current API nested options cause false positive
File text does not bind routes to server
No default or reverse-proxy configuration knowledge
rules.wording: Server-start-shaped call lacks a direct body-limit label. This heuristic does not inspect nested options; review actual server configuration before acting.

rules.trigger: upgrade_websocket/ws_upgrade lacks origin or allowed_origins labels and mocket/crescent import hint
rules.real_evidence: No matching API declarations found in reviewed mocket 0.9.1 or crescent 0.11.0; synthetic calls only
limitations: No real current-library API validation
Prior middleware validation invisible
Label presence is not validation proof
rules.wording: WebSocket-upgrade-shaped call lacks origin labels. Confirm a real upgrade API and inspect origin validation across middleware.

rules.trigger: String + operands with path/input-like variable names or slash literal
rules.real_evidence: Actual builtin string concatenation compiles; constant-valued locals still match
limitations: Variable names do not prove user control
No filesystem sink or normalization semantics
Path joining alone is not path traversal
rules.wording: Concatenation uses path/input-like names. Review any filesystem use, source trust and containment checks.

rules.trigger: unsafe_to*/unsafe_from*/unsafe_new/unsafe_cast names outside any guard body; unsafe_to_char/byte excluded
rules.real_evidence: No matched dangerous public builtin API validated; synthetic harmless unsafe_cast compiles and matches
limitations: Arbitrary guard suppresses without proving precondition
Function name does not establish unsafe semantics
Many genuine unsafe APIs are excluded
rules.wording: Call name suggests an unchecked operation. Confirm the declaration and its preconditions; current guard filtering does not prove safety.

rules.trigger: panic/abort name except guard else, unwrap-like functions, filename/text exclusions
rules.real_evidence: Real builtin abort compiles; reachable guard abort is filtered; local harmless abort binding also matches
limitations: No reachability analysis
String contents and function names are not safety proofs
Platform file exclusion hides compiled target behavior
Local binding unresolved
rules.wording: Call named panic/abort may terminate execution if it resolves to the builtin. Review reachability and input conditions; filtered locations are not proven safe.

rules.trigger: cast/reinterpret_cast dot method, except any file containing extern JS or #external text
rules.real_evidence: Only synthetic harmless custom cast method validated in this audit; no canonical unsafe library cast proven
limitations: No receiver or declaration identity
File-wide extern substring suppresses unrelated calls
Custom safe conversions match
rules.wording: Method name suggests a cast. Resolve its declaration and conversion guarantees before treating it as a type-safety issue.
